title: Review: the twelve uncovered synthetic_reference execution records - fabricated run windows, unretained synthetic evidence, and specificity of each blocked reason
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft' rather than 'reviewed' or 'approved': this record is the output of an automated review pass and no human reviewer has confirmed it. automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation only and is not a statement about engineering validity.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Covers the twelve synthetic_reference execution records that no review record enumerated. Reviewed for the honesty of execution_kind and outcome, whether any record asserts a run that did not occur, whether unretained synthetic evidence is declared as such, the specificity of each blocked reason, and the resolution of every identifier named. Three defects recorded: FB2-REV-FND-000044 (all eight blocked records assert a fabricated run window), FB2-REV-FND-000045 (the four synthetic_fixture pass records are consistent with the evidence gap already recorded at FB2-REV-FND-000143), and FB2-REV-FND-000046 (the coverage dimension cannot span both profiles of a shared identifier, which is why this coverage was split across two records). Passing checks are recorded under results_summary.checks_that_passed_and_are_not_findings.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: Adds FB2-REV-FND-000047 and nothing else. The finding was produced by an independent whole-corpus check written from scratch for this pass, which imports nothing from corpus.py and compares each review's own reviewed_ids set against the set of targets its own reviewed_by links name. That check found this disagreement and the shipped corpus-wide comparison did not, because set equality cannot distinguish a correct pairing of reviews to artefacts from an incorrect one. The finding is disclosed as arising from that independent check rather than from this record's own twelve in-scope records, none of which is among the ten artefacts the disagreement concerns, and the scope, the twelve reviewed_ids digests and the three findings recorded at revision 1 are untouched. The new finding's own provenance is stated in its description. corpus.py gained reviewed_by_attribution_agrees_per_review and reviewed_by_attribution_mismatches so the disagreement is reported on every run rather than being rediscovered by hand; both are reported and neither gates.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No human reviewer has read this record, and human_approval_status remains pending; production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

scope: Complete review, not a sample, of the twelve synthetic_reference execution records that no review record enumerated: FB2-VER-EXE-000002, -000003, -000004 and -000005 (four identifiers also carried by an as_is record about a DIFFERENT subject, covered by FB2-REV-000016), and FB2-VER-EXE-000021 through FB2-VER-EXE-000028 (eight records, identifiers not shared with any other profile). The twenty-eight execution records already covered by FB2-REV-000006 and FB2-REV-000007, and the four as_is records covered by FB2-REV-000016, are outside this record's scope and are explicitly not claimed to have been reviewed here. The rest of the corpus is outside this record's scope. This record and FB2-REV-000016 together cover the sixteen uncovered execution records; they are two halves of one review, not two independent reviews, and FB2-REV-FND-000046 records why the split was necessary.
review_method: Per-record reading of all twelve. For each: execution_kind and outcome compared against the evidence the record actually retains; every test_measure_id and evidence_refs entry resolved against the artifact index; the timestamps block compared against the record's own limitations and against whether any run occurred; each blocked_reason and what_would_unblock_it read for specificity rather than for presence; and the filesystem enumerated at docs/artifacts/evidence/synthetic-fixtures/ to test the four unretained-evidence claims rather than accept them. The grep for the word 'timestamp' across all twelve limitations arrays is reported as a measured zero in results_summary rather than as an impression.

findings.description: This record reports a zero-duration run for work that demonstrably happened. It carries execution_kind none and outcome blocked, which is correct and is not what this finding disputes: the unit test was not executed, because its include closure needs three HALCoGen-generated TI headers that this host cannot produce. But the same record retains real, hash-verified evidence of real work: docs/artifacts/evidence/actual-runs/foxbms2-host-unit-test-macos-2026-09-29/halcogen-dependency-closure.json, whose sha256 matches the recorded output_hashes.halcogen_dependency_closure and whose logs[0].hash, and which contains a derivation over 313 unit-test source files, identifies 136 of them as having no HALCoGen dependency, and names the 33 distinct HALCoGen headers the tree requires. A process walked 313 files and wrote a file. Reporting timestamps.start == timestamps.end and duration_ms 0 alongside that evidence is internally inconsistent: the record's own output asserts work while its timing fields deny any elapsed time. The anomaly the record does record - that macOS is not a supported host platform, established by reading cli/cmd_embedded_ut/embedded_ut_impl.py - is the right anomaly and is well evidenced. The timing fields are the part that is wrong.
findings.evidence: FB2-VER-EXE-000004 output_hashes.halcogen_dependency_closure = sha256:df51a921954ace7f5d3f897dea1ff595cf675d6fd09629cdeda6deb65dc0f7a3; the named evidence file exists and its recomputed sha256 is identical. The file records total_tests 313, tests_with_no_halcogen_dependency 136, distinct_halcogen_headers of 33 entries. The same record's timestamps are {start: 2026-09-29T08:13:21Z, end: 2026-09-29T08:13:21Z, duration_ms: 0}. Its limitations read 'Not executed: HALCoGen-generated TI headers unavailable on this host', which is true of the test and silent on the timing fields.

findings.description: The four synthetic_fixture execution records in this scope that report outcome pass carry no retained evidence, and the corpus handles this honestly, which is why this is recorded as a confirmation and not a new defect. Each has logs [] and no evidence file, and each carries a provenance_repair entry naming unretained_evidence and recording that the previous build/synthetic/*.log reference was removed rather than replaced. A reader is therefore told, in the record itself, that the narrated pass has no artefact behind it. This review checked the claim rather than accepting it: docs/artifacts/evidence/synthetic-fixtures/ holds no fixture artefact, only a MANIFEST.md, so the records' account of their own evidence matches the filesystem. The underlying weakness - a narrated synthetic pass with nothing retained - was already raised at FB2-REV-FND-000143 by the pass that reviewed the covered executions. What this review adds is the confirmation that the four records outside that earlier scope are consistent with it rather than a second, differently-worded instance.
findings.evidence: FB2-VER-EXE-000002, FB2-VER-EXE-000003, FB2-VER-EXE-000004 and FB2-VER-EXE-000005 in the synthetic_reference profile each carry execution_kind synthetic_fixture, outcome pass, logs [], and a provenance_repair containing unretained_evidence. Enumeration of docs/artifacts/evidence/synthetic-fixtures/ finds MANIFEST.md and no fixture artefact.

findings.description: The automated_review_coverage dimension cannot express coverage of both profiles' records under a shared identifier, and the sixteen uncovered execution records had to be covered by two review records rather than one for that reason. A review record carries one `profile`, and every entry in its reviewed_ids resolves against the artifact index in THAT profile - so a record cannot simultaneously hold the digest of the as_is FB2-VER-EXE-000002 and the digest of the synthetic_reference FB2-VER-EXE-000002, which are different files with different content. The first attempt at this review did exactly that and produced sixteen review_digest_mismatch errors, because the resolver correctly resolved all sixteen entries to the synthetic_reference copies. The condition is not limited to executions: thirty-nine identifiers are shared across profiles (FB2-SAF-VOC-000001, identifier_vocabulary.migration_decision_2026_10_03), so any future review that needs to span both profiles' records of the same identifier must be split. The split has a cost a reader should know about: the two halves of one logical review are two records with two revision histories, and nothing in the coverage dimension says they belong together.
findings.evidence: FB2-REV-000016 reviewed_ids holds 4 entries with profile as_is and FB2-REV-000017 holds 12 with profile synthetic_reference; the 16 identifiers together are FB2-VER-EXE-000002..000005 in both profiles plus FB2-VER-EXE-000021..000028. FB2-REV-000016 declares profile as_is and its reviewed_ids therefore cannot carry the synthetic_reference digests for the four shared identifiers. corpus.py resolves reviewed_ids digests against the reviewing record's own profile, which is why the unsplit record failed with review_digest_mismatch on FB2-VER-EXE-000002 through FB2-VER-EXE-000005. The finding is recorded against FB2-VER-EXE-000002 because that identifier is one of the four that forced the split: a review.schema.json finding requires an artifact_id matching ^FB2-[A-Z]{2,3}-[A-Z]{2,3}-[0-9]{6}$, so a review record cannot be named as the subject of its own finding.

findings.description: Two records disagree about which review covered ten artefacts, and the corpus's own agreement gate cannot see it. FB2-REV-000015 enumerates FB2-VER-EXE-000016 through FB2-VER-EXE-000020 and FB2-VER-TMS-000016 through FB2-VER-TMS-000020 in its reviewed_ids, while the reviewed_by links for all ten name FB2-REV-000013 as the source. A reader who follows the traceability graph reaches FB2-REV-000013 and a reader who reads the review record reaches FB2-REV-000015; one of them is wrong and the corpus does not say which. The existing gate misses it because automated_review_coverage.reviewed_by_agrees_with_records compares the two sources corpus-wide as SETS of ids. Ten ids linked from one review and ten different ids claimed by another leave both corpus-wide sets identical, so the field is True and the check passes. The detail text - 'reviewed_by links and reviewed_ids name the same set' - is true of the sets and reads as though it were true of the attribution, which is the stronger claim a reader will take from it. This is a review-coverage traceability defect, not an evidence defect: nothing here says a review was not performed, only that the two records of who performed it disagree.
findings.evidence: FB2-REV-000015 (profile synthetic_reference) reviewed_ids names FB2-VER-EXE-000016, -000017, -000018, -000019, -000020, FB2-VER-TMS-000016, -000017, -000018, -000019 and -000020. The reviewed_by links for each of those ten target_ids carry source_id FB2-REV-000013. Measured on 2026-10-03: corpus-wide reviewed_by_agrees_with_records is True while the per-review comparison disagrees in both directions - FB2-REV-000013 links ten ids it does not claim and FB2-REV-000015 claims ten ids it does not link. Note the symmetric shape: this is not one record with ten stale links, it is one review's link set and another review's claim set describing the same ten artefacts differently, which is why a set comparison cannot distinguish a correct pairing from an incorrect one.

dispositions.action: Accepted as a real evidence-honesty defect, and NOT remediated by this review. The honest fix is to stop asserting a window that did not occur: either omit timestamps on a record with no run, or introduce and use an explicit absent marker for the timestamp field as the corpus already does for evidence hashes. Writing that marker is a vocabulary change to execution.schema.json and a decision about what a consumer should see in place of a timestamp, which is a corpus-owner decision rather than a review finding to apply unilaterally. Escalated for a corpus owner. This review changed no execution record.

Accepted as a confirmation that the four synthetic_fixture records outside the earlier pass's scope are consistent with the evidence gap already recorded at FB2-REV-FND-000143, not as a new defect needing new remediation. The underlying gap remains open on the earlier finding and is not closed here.

Accepted as a structural limitation of the review-coverage dimension, disclosed rather than worked around silently. It is not remediated here: making a review record able to span two profiles for the same identifier would mean giving reviewed_ids a per-entry profile, which changes the review schema and the digest-resolution rule, and is a corpus-owner decision. This review split the coverage into FB2-REV-000016 and this record instead, and says so in both scopes so that a reader counting reviews does not mistake two records for two independent opinions.

Deferred, and deliberately not repaired by this review. Which of the two records is right is a fact about the two review passes that produced them, and neither record carries a revision_history entry that would let a reader decide. Repairing it would mean either re-attributing ten links to FB2-REV-000015 or deleting ten entries from FB2-REV-000015's reviewed_ids, and this review examined neither FB2-REV-000013 nor FB2-REV-000015: both are outside its scope and their subject matter is not this review's. What this review does instead is make the disagreement impossible to overlook: corpus.py now computes and reports automated_review_coverage.reviewed_by_attribution_agrees_per_review and reviewed_by_attribution_mismatches on every run. The trigger that would bring this back is a decision by the owner of those two reviews recording which pass covered the ten artefacts.

limitations: This review did not modify any execution record. Every defect it found is left open on the record it names, and nothing here is a remediation.

It did not read the repository test tree, the Ceedling configuration or the HALCoGen inputs, so it takes no position on whether any blocked execution is correctly blocked on the merits. It checked only that each record's account of its own blocker is specific and that its evidence claims match the filesystem.
It did not judge whether any of the twelve measures is the right measure for the requirement it verifies. A wrong-but-honestly-recorded execution passes every check this review makes.

Each of four of these identifiers is carried by two records, one per profile. This record resolved every reference in the synthetic_reference profile only, and the as_is siblings are covered by FB2-REV-000016. That split is structural and is recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000046.

coverage is a count, not a certificate. Naming these twelve records in reviewed_ids asserts that they were read and checked against the checklist above, and asserts nothing about the other records no review covers.

checks_that_passed_and_are_not_findings.all_identifiers_resolve: 12 of 12 records. Every test_measure_id and every evidence_refs entry carrying an FB2- identifier resolves against the artifact index in the synthetic_reference profile.
checks_that_passed_and_are_not_findings.unretained_evidence_claim_matches_the_fi: The four synthetic_fixture pass records state they retain no evidence. Enumeration of docs/artifacts/evidence/synthetic-fixtures/ finds MANIFEST.md and no fixture artefact, so the claim is accurate.
checks_that_passed_and_are_not_findings.blocked_records_name_a_specific_blocker: 8 of 8. Each names a concrete blocker rather than a generic one - missing HALCoGen headers, a harness that would require writing into the repository test tree, a subject absent from the pinned source, an oracle that is a declared assumption - and each lists concrete unblocking conditions. FB2-VER-EXE-000027 states that its measure's subject does not exist at all, which is the correct disposition.
checks_that_passed_and_are_not_findings.nothing_in_this_group_overstates_what_wa: All twelve carry human_approval_status pending, production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, and the eight blocked records additionally carry outcome blocked with execution_kind none.
checks_that_passed_and_are_not_findings.why_not_findings: A review that reported only defects would misrepresent this group.
